environment.cpu: Intel Core i9-11900KF (8 cores, 16 threads), CPU E-steps use all hardware threads
environment.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 (8 GiB), driver 590.48.01, subgroup 32, shader float64
environment.display: Xephyr :7 (nested X server), 64x64 window, VSync off, validation layers off

outcomes.rigid_100000_points: Vulkan 19.8 s vs CPU twin 184.7 s (9.3x), Auto 187.7 s, Nystroem 121.0 s, dense 411.0 s; 21 of 48 iterations on the device (9 under the whole-iteration guard)
outcomes.rigid_10000_points: Vulkan 399 ms vs CPU twin 1324 ms (3.3x); 19 of 35 on the device
outcomes.rigid_1000_points: Vulkan 78 ms vs CPU twin 27 ms: frame latency dominates
outcomes.cpu_rows: 0 on every run: the fixture's far (clutter) rows carry negligible kernel mass against the uniform term, so the gain here comes entirely from the float-float coordinates removing the coordinate-rounding term; per-row CPU evaluation is exercised by the two-cluster fixture in the unit test and the gpu;vulkan smoke (1 CPU row)
outcomes.parity: max registered-point delta to the CPU twin 2.5e-11 (10^5); RMS to the ground truth equal

limitations: The per-row estimate is first order, not rigorous. One host, one GPU, one rigid fixture; frame latency still loses small inputs (GRAPHICS-150).
not_measured: Nonrigid and Bayesian device runs; memory peak; other GPUs; a scaling fixture that needs CPU rows.
